before_state.description:
## Problem

Authority and ROE state is projected (<issue id="09fd8608-86ec-4243-888d-7dd0f126a8d2" label="DRG-182" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-182/project-command-authority-and-rules-of-engagement-state" />, <issue id="62f19a5c-38c2-44cb-ad50-c2e2ba23b291" label="DRG-209" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-209/slice-a-headless-authority-and-roe-projection" />), and WRA salvo-remaining shows on weapon chrome (<issue id="b052e2f4-59ae-43a4-850f-ae28460de62f" label="DRG-259" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-259/c2-02-wra-salvo-remaining-on-weapon-chrome" />). But the player cannot see *where* a unit's effective doctrine, ROE, or WRA value comes from (side, mission, group, or unit override), or reset an override back to inherited. In CMO this inheritance view is the main way a player finds out why a unit held fire or fired unexpectedly.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual §3.3.12: every doctrine option has an "inherited" setting. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>)
* CMO manual §6.3.8: side doctrine/ROE/WRA is set at the top level and "flows down to mission and then groups/units". The WRA tab lists every weapon the side uses. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/drop-down-menus/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/drop-down-menus/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="9cb22a1c-4d7a-499d-ba6d-44462898cedd" label="DRG-321" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-321/jev-vs3-roe-noul-facade-accept-coordinationcommandbridge" /> (ROE Noul + façade Accept) is about AI-assisted ROE suggestions, not showing inheritance. No issue covers per-level provenance or reset.

## Acceptance criteria

* A headless `DoctrineInheritanceProjection` gives, for each selected unit and each doctrine/ROE/WRA field: the effective value, the source level (Side/Mission/Group/Unit), and the overridden parent value if there is one.
* Reset-to-inherited is sent as a command through the command façade and recorded in the order log. It is never a UI-side state mutation.

before_state.title: Multi-target manual weapon allocation plan with per-weapon can-fire reasons
before_state.description:
## Problem

The attack-options menu (<issue id="edefdae9-4a5b-49dc-ba94-cc0d4a461203" label="DRG-262" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-262/c2-05-attack-options-menu-preview-parity" />) previews one shooter against one target. There is no way to build a manual allocation plan across several selected targets and shooters: N weapons per target, with a per-weapon "OK, can fire" or a specific reason it can't. CMO's manual allocation dialog (Shift+F1) is the main player tool for coordinated strikes and for learning weapon limits.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual §3 (Engage Target(s) Manual): drag-select multiple targets, pick an attacker, and see suitable weapons grouped by type. Legal weapons that are outside firing parameters show the reason in red; valid ones show "OK - Can fire". You allocate a quantity per target, and allocations show both per attacker and per target. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>) and [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/05-3-shortcut-buttons-and-windows/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/05-3-shortcut-buttons-and-windows/>)
* CMO combat chapter: manual assignment is "a very effective method of getting good feedback on weaponry limitations", because the crew runs an exhaustive checklist of conditions. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="edefdae9-4a5b-49dc-ba94-cc0d4a461203" label="DRG-262" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-262/c2-05-attack-options-menu-preview-parity" /> is single-target preview parity, <issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" /> covers abort codes in the engage explanation, <issue id="0f26c476-2643-4cb9-b689-d068770f58bd" label="DRG-172" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-172/add-threat-assessment-and-weapon-recommendation" /> covers recommendations, and <issue id="8d85d519-5cec-4c0a-a35a-63206eb9d6cc" label="DRG-224" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-224/slice-b-headless-magazine-and-salvo-employment-ledger" /> is the employment ledger. None covers a multi-target allocation plan.

## Acceptance criteria

* A headless `AllocationPlanProjection` takes {shooters\[\], targets\[\], allocations\[\]} and returns, for each (shooter, weapon, target): Can-fire, or a domain `FireAbortReason` code reused from <issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" />. It also returns per-target and per-shooter totals and the remaining magazine count from the <issue id="8d85d519-5cec-4c0a-a35a-63206eb9d6cc" label="DRG-224" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-224/slice-b-headless-magazine-and-salvo-employment-ledger" /> ledger.
* Committing a plan sends ordinary engage commands through the command façade. The projection itself never fires and does not touch the DelegationBridge Tick/hotpath.
* The UI lists allocations by attacker and by target. Reasons use the same text source as <issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" />/<issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" />.
* Over-allocation beyond the magazine is rejected with a reason before commit.
* Tests cover a 2×3 plan, a mixed can-fire/abort result, an over-allocation reject, and replay determinism of the committed orders.

There is no way to build a manual allocation plan across several selected targets and shooters: N weapons per target, with a per-weapon "OK, can fire" or a specific reason it can't. CMO's manual allocation dialog (Shift+F1) is the main player tool for coordinated strikes and for learning weapon limits.

## Evidence/Research

* CMO manual §3 (Engage Target(s) Manual): drag-select multiple targets, pick an attacker, and see suitable weapons grouped by type. Legal weapons that are outside firing parameters show the reason in red; valid ones show "OK - Can fire". You allocate a quantity per target, and allocations show both per attacker and per target. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/user-interface/>) and [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/05-3-shortcut-buttons-and-windows/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/05-3-shortcut-buttons-and-windows/>)
* CMO combat chapter: manual assignment is "a very effective method of getting good feedback on weaponry limitations", because the crew runs an exhaustive checklist of conditions. [https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/](<https://command.matrixgames.com/manual/combat/>)
* Existing backlog: <issue id="edefdae9-4a5b-49dc-ba94-cc0d4a461203" label="DRG-262" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-262/c2-05-attack-options-menu-preview-parity" /> is single-target preview parity, <issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" /> covers abort codes in the engage explanation, <issue id="0f26c476-2643-4cb9-b689-d068770f58bd" label="DRG-172" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-172/add-threat-assessment-and-weapon-recommendation" /> covers recommendations, and <issue id="8d85d519-5cec-4c0a-a35a-63206eb9d6cc" label="DRG-224" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-224/slice-b-headless-magazine-and-salvo-employment-ledger" /> is the employment ledger. None covers a multi-target allocation plan.

## Acceptance criteria

* A headless `AllocationPlanProjection` takes {shooters\[\], targets\[\], allocations\[\]} and returns, for each (shooter, weapon, target): Can-fire, or a domain `FireAbortReason` code reused from <issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" />. It also returns per-target and per-shooter totals and the remaining magazine count from the <issue id="8d85d519-5cec-4c0a-a35a-63206eb9d6cc" label="DRG-224" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-224/slice-b-headless-magazine-and-salvo-employment-ledger" /> ledger.
* Committing a plan sends ordinary engage commands through the command façade. The projection itself never fires and does not touch the DelegationBridge Tick/hotpath.
* The UI lists allocations by attacker and by target. Reasons use the same text source as <issue id="4d622922-9423-4af4-aa9b-1aff30bf0146" label="DRG-168" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-168/build-engagement-explanation-surface" />/<issue id="077bcad5-8b44-4c82-9f04-cdcff7dfa3df" label="DRG-265" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-265/c2-14-domain-abort-codes-in-engage-explain-chrome" />.
* Over-allocation beyond the magazine is rejected with a reason before commit.
* Tests cover a 2×3 plan, a mixed can-fire/abort result, an over-allocation reject, and replay determinism of the committed orders.

Origin: Projects Manager web research 2026-10-07

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo

## Definition of Ready (Hygiene, 2026-10-29)

Verified at `main` [`3bcfbb7b`](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/3bcfbb7bede990c6d855b56f5f32b89329334ee2>). Status unchanged (Backlog). Scoping and Surface stay with CMANO.

ADR-010 command façade.
* **Size note:** headless `AllocationPlanProjection` and the UI may ship as two PRs (\~400 changed lines is guidance); the AC above already separates them.

before_state.title: Wire ObserverModeChromePresentation into C2TopBarPanelHost.Refresh and command hosts (make DRG-249 observer chrome player-visible)
before_state.description:
Follow-up deferred from [PR #709](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/709>) (DRG-249), review thread PRRT_kwDOSqtCp86pxSCu.

`ObserverModeChromePresentation` is currently used only in its own file and tests. This item makes the observer chrome visible to players when `AttachReplayViewer` is on.

## Scope

* `C2TopBarPanelHost.Refresh` currently renders `DelegationBridgeHost.LastTopBar`; bind the observer/read-only mode label and disabled controls from `ObserverModeChromePresentation`.
* The live command handlers call `C2PlayerCommandBridge` directly; route them through the observer projection so order/delegation controls are disabled in observer mode.
* Surface the `TryIssueOrder` refusal reason visibly to the player.

**Constraint:** Touching `DelegationBridgeHost` needs a CMANO Surface stamp plus the owner's OK (adjacent to the DelegationBridge hard-no).

**Surface (CMANO 2026-10-14, main 254d2c96):** `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/C2TopBarPanelHost.cs`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Presentation/ObserverModeChromePresentation.cs`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Presentation/ObserverModeChromePresentationTests.cs`, `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/UI/TopBar/C2TopBarPanel.uss`. Read-only: `DelegationBridgeHost.cs`, `C2PlayerCommandBridge.cs`, `C2TopBarProjection.cs`.

before_state.title: Verify off-grid gating works when mvpEngagement=false (follow-up from #713)
before_state.description:
Deferred from [PR #713](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/713>) (DRG-379/386/390), Codex P2 review thread PRRT_kwDOSqtCp86pyIb6: "Initialize off-grid state when engagement is disabled".

The original concern: with `commsGrid` transitions but `mvpEngagement: false`, `Session` was null, so the off-grid check always returned false and off-grid units still accepted orders. Off-grid membership is a comms rule, not an engagement feature. The gating has since moved out of `DelegationBridge.cs` into the orchestrator/command façade (`DelegationOrchestrator.CommsGrid`, `C2PlayerCommandBridge`), but that path has not been verified for `mvpEngagement=false`.

## Acceptance

* Add a verification test: scenario with `commsGrid` transitions, constructed with `mvpEngagement: false`; an off-grid unit's new direct orders, attack options and direct-control requests are refused with `FireAbortReason.OffGrid`, and back-on-grid restores them.
* If the test fails, fix it in the orchestrator/façade layer.
* **Must not touch the DelegationBridge hotpath** (`DelegationBridge.cs` / Tick); any `DelegationBridgeHost` or `SimulationSession` change needs a CMANO Surface stamp plus the owner's OK.
* Replay hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged; no ReplayGolden re-bless.

before_state.title: CommsGrid registry engine position feed (DRG-390 follow-up from #713)
before_state.description:
Follow-up deferred from [PR #713](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/713>) (merged `3f5ae73f`; DRG-379/386/390), listed under "Follow-ups (not in this PR)".

`CommsGridRegistry.ReportPosition(unitId, simTick, lat, lon)` exists and freezes reports while a unit is off grid, but only tests call it (`CommsGridRegistryTests`, `OffGridCommandFacadeTests`). In real sessions, `CommsGridProjection`'s last-reported position stays empty, so DRG-390's "UI shows the last-reported position" AC is only met in tests. `ObservedState` carries no positions, and `DelegationOrchestrator.Tick` advances the grid without unit kinematics.

## Scope

* After kinematics each tick, report unit positions to the registry in unit-id ordinal order.
* No RNG; scenarios without a `commsGrid` section are unaffected.

## Acceptance

* In a Baltic harness scenario with `commsGrid`, the last-reported position freezes at the off-grid tick and resumes after OnGrid.
* Replay hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged; no ReplayGolden re-bless.

## Hard-no

The likely wiring point is `SimulationSession.RunExecutingTick` (**hard-no**): needs owner GO plus a CMANO Surface stamp. `DelegationBridge.cs` / Tick stays zero-touch.

Design notes: `docs/engineering/los-eccm-offgrid.md`.

**Surface (CMANO 2026-10-14, main 254d2c96):** `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/SimulationSession.cs` (only the post-kinematics position report in `RunExecutingTick`), `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Orchestration/OrchestratorOffGridTests.cs`, new `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Orchestration/SimulationSessionCommsGridPositionFeedTests.cs`. Read-only: `CommsGridRegistry.cs`, `CommsGridProjection.cs`, `DelegationOrchestrator.cs`, `docs/engineering/los-eccm-offgrid.md`. `DelegationBridge.cs` / Tick stays zero-touch.

Coordinator-only shared-file edits, in one PR:

* `src/ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli/Program.cs`: one new `case "aar_explain"` that calls a thin command class.

Blocked by the AAR pipeline issue.

## Problem

`IHindsightMemoryClient` documents retain, recall, and reflect, but exposes only retain and reflect. `HindsightSessionFinalizer.ReflectAarAsync` discards its result and swallows failures, so a completed reflection is never visible to anyone.

The first AAR slice reads the exported evidence file and needs neither fix. This issue is the follow-up.

## Scope

* Add a separate recall interface in the host adapter. Do not change `IHindsightMemoryClient`.
* Add a new awaitable finalize method beside `OnScenarioFinalized` that returns the reflection result.
* Leave `OnScenarioFinalized` and its fire-and-forget teardown behaviour untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Existing Hindsight tests pass unmodified.
2. With the sidecar unreachable, the new method returns an explicit unavailable status and simulation teardown is unaffected.
3. Order-log fingerprints and replay hashes unchanged with Hindsight on, off, or unreachable.
4. Both targets (`net11.0` and `netstandard2.1`) build.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the AAR pipeline. Lower priority than the rest of slice 2.

Scoping: CMANO adds Surface before Todo.

>>> Agent notes

Proposed surface (not a CMANO stamp): recall adapter under `src/ProjectAegis.Ai.Host/Memory/**` (new). The awaitable finalize is an **additive** method in `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Hindsight/HindsightSessionFinalizer.cs`; this is the only issue in the epic that edits an existing shared-project file, so run GitNexus impact on `OnScenarioFinalized` first (older index: LOW, 2 direct dependents) and get a CMANO Surface stamp.

Read-only: `IHindsightMemoryClient.cs`, `HindsightHttpMemoryClient.cs`, `docs/engineering/hindsight-session-memory-sidecar.md`.

>>>

before_state.description:
Follow-up from Security scanner and Jev on <pull-request id="9aa03ff2-8ea7-47fd-b894-a85bbee4b7be" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#870" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/drg-766-port-buildkite-ci-onto-github-actions-self-hosted-runners-a0f10fcb16b1" /> (head cd92ee5).

* Verify the downloaded .NET SDK archive with sha512. [dotnet-install.sh](<http://dotnet-install.sh>) is already pinned, but pinning the installer doesn't pin the SDK bytes.
* unity-ci.yml hardening, kept out of #870 because it was gated: persist-credentials: false and a job timeout.
* Any remaining LOW items from Security scanner's #870 verdict.

**Constraints:** draft PR only. No ready, no merge, no workflow_dispatch. Change unity-ci.yml only with Jev's sign-off, and keep replay hash 17144800277401907079.

**Security scanner LOW items at cd92ee5 (verdict PASS-WITH-CONDITIONS):**

1. gitnexus-wiki push (:65). Use the AUTHORIZATION: basic base64(x-access-token:TOKEN) header, not bearer. With enforce_admins on, branch protection blocks a direct push to main, so push a branch and open a PR, or drop the step. The step also still runs an unpinned `npm i -g gitnexus` (:33).
2. Set npm_config_cache to RUNNER_TEMP for the gitnexus tarball install, and consider --ignore-scripts.
3. Pin node exactly in the gitnexus jobs (Node 24), and skip the unchecked download fallback in [agent-bootstrap-node.sh](<http://agent-bootstrap-node.sh>).
4. Vendor [dotnet-install.sh](<http://dotnet-install.sh>) so an upstream update doesn't break the hash check.
5. Remove the redundant setup-dotnet in selfhosted-ci.yml (:51, :110).

PR <pull-request id="1e443860-106b-409d-ab13-ec351a172305" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#669" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/featui-drg-264-contact-list-sortfilter-fog-mode-briefing-label-303bcb7f65f7" /> added `using ProjectAegis.Sim.Scenario` to Unity `C2TopBarPanelHost.cs` and reads `Orchestrator.ScenarioPolicy.PlayerInfoModel` directly (`ResolvePlayerInfoModel`, \~lines 515–518) for fog-mode chrome. That bypasses [ADR-010](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/main/docs/architecture/adr-010-headless-first-command-driven-ui.md>) §3 (presentation consumes read-only projections).

Recorded as [DRG-771](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-771>) §8 item 8 (CMA-32). Owner go (7:40 PM CT Nov 16, phrase **Accept jev's calls**) chose **waive as read-only presentation use** with a **low-priority exit ticket** to route the read through a projection — not an immediate Unity change in the waiver PR.

## Waiver (docs only — this ticket is the exit)

Temporary waiver lives at:

`docs/architecture/waivers/waiver-c2-topbar-sim-read-2026-11-16.md`

ADR-010 status stays **Accepted**; this waiver does not amend the ADR.

## Required fix (implementation)

1. Expose `PlayerInfoModel` (or equivalent fog/info-model field) on a headless projection the top bar already binds (prefer extending an existing top-bar / loop-policy projection).
2. Update `C2TopBarPanelHost` to consume that projection only; remove `using ProjectAegis.Sim.Scenario` and direct `ScenarioPolicy` / `PlayerInfoModel` type use from the host.
3. Keep the path **read-only** (ADR-010 §2–3). No writes into Sim/Delegation; no `DelegationBridge` hotpath, `SimulationSession`, `CatalogWriteGate`, or `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` edits under this ticket unless separately reserved.

* Expanding other Unity → Sim imports (including `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` baseline)
* Amending ADR-010 text/status
* Live Editor-only chrome polish without a projection contract

* Parent audit: [DRG-771](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-771>)
* Disjoint from [DRG-772](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-772>) (MissionEditor.Cli → [Ai.Host](<http://Ai.Host>) / ADR-030)

`unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/C2TopBarPanelHost.cs ; matching projection / binder / *Tests under UnityAdapter or Presentation ; no DelegationBridge / SimulationSession / CatalogWriteGate / MapPlaceholderPanelHost`

## Done when

1. Top bar fog/info-model chrome binds a projection, not `Orchestrator.ScenarioPolicy` from Unity.
2. `C2TopBarPanelHost.cs` has no `ProjectAegis.Sim.Scenario` import.
3. Waiver marked exited with implementing PR link.
4. Headless gates green; Unity MCP noted if Editor/visual proof is required.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### PRD-P0-1 — Glass-cockpit fixed layout & 1600x900 density budget (lines 74-74)

Fixed layout with 7 panels (units, contacts, map ADR-007 Phase A, weapons, missions, log, attention) continuously reachable at min 1600x900 @ 100%; map >= 50% viewport; roster/log/attention >= 8 rows; font >= 12px.

- [ ] \[PRD-P0-1\] Wireframe sign-off (OQ-2) by ux-designer + user-experience-military-analyst; scripted walkthrough at 1600x900 meets density budget.

### PRD-P0-5 — Typed order line + direct manipulation command symmetry (lines 78-78)

Single command grammar (MVP: Move, Hold, Engage, SetEwPosture, ReturnToBase), single validation path, single result presentation (accepted/rejected/pending); rejection preserves draft & selection.

- [ ] \[PRD-P0-5\] UI-05 / UI-06 / §3.7; command-adapter integration + UI/controller tests prove typed & direct manipulation emit identical canonical command.

Compression control; auto-pause with visible reason on first detection of hostile/unknown contact and own-side loss/damage; explicit resume; pause events carry raid/formation grouping keys at P0; precedence pause > forced-1x > player compression.

- [ ] \[PRD-P0-7\] UI-08 / §3.3; time-control integration test + dense-scenario walkthrough recording pauses/min.

### PRD-P0-12 — Unit drill-down drawer via extended UnitDetailProjection (lines 85-85)

Extend UnitDetailProjection to compose identity/class, position/course/speed/altitude, fuel, sensor states+EMCON, weapons/magazine, current orders+mission, effective ROE/doctrine, damage/readiness; UI binds to projection only.

- [ ] \[PRD-P0-12\] Selecting any unit opens drawer with all listed facets bound to live projections; UI binding test.

### PRD-NFR-1 — Localization externalization (keys + parameters, no hardcoded text) (lines 89-89)

Externalize all player-facing strings from day one; sim/delegation-emitted rejection reasons, validation errors, and DecisionLog summaries surfaced as localizable keys + parameters (OQ-3).

- [ ] \[PRD-NFR-1\] Zero hardcoded player-facing strings; sim/delegation error/summary outputs use key+parameter format.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### FR-19 — Platform and Catalog Editor (Excel Write-Gate Round-Trip) (lines 154-154)

Enable clean-room platform and catalog authoring via Excel workbook export/import/diff routed through the extend-only CatalogWriteGate per 21-Platform-Editor.md and ADR-011 (tracker status: MVP-done / Partial+).

- [ ] \[FR-19\] IPlatformWorkbookIo, PlatformWorkbookExporter/Importer/Diff round-trip platform data through CatalogWriteGate Propose/Approve.
- [ ] \[FR-19\] Remaining live Unity Editor polish and screenshot evidence complete per 21-Platform-Editor.md.

### OV-NFR-03 — Clean-Room Product and Auditable Data NFR (lines 47-51)

Clean-room architecture NFR (also NFR line 161): reuse observable patterns only (no proprietary CMO DB/code/scenarios/manuals), treat database and scenario systems as auditable first-class products, and keep agent outputs reviewable, reversible, and evidence-linked.

- [ ] \[OV-NFR-03\] Catalog and scenario intake uses clean-room fixtures, workbooks, and OSINT evidence links without proprietary CMO artifacts.
- [ ] \[OV-NFR-03\] Agent-generated catalog/scenario outputs remain reviewable, reversible, and evidence-linked.

### OV-NFR-06 — Data and Scenario Moddability Scope (v1) (lines 168-168)

Support database and scenario modding at v1 via published SQLite schema and scenario JSON format aligned with clean-room community-evidence intake; code/plugin modding is out of scope for v1.

- [ ] \[OV-NFR-06\] SQLite catalog schema and scenario JSON format are documented and loadable for community scenarios/databases without engine fork.
- [ ] \[OV-NFR-06\] Arbitrary C# code/plugin modding remains excluded in v1.

### OV-SCOPE-01 — Shipped Vertical Slice and Active Editor Program Scope (lines 62-85)

Deliver the Baltic theater v2/v3 vertical slice and active post-S80 scenario/platform authoring programs while treating additional regional theaters (Black Sea, South China Sea) as future data extensibility.

- [ ] \[OV-SCOPE-01\] Baltic v2/v3 slice, headless sim/delegation, clean-room write gate, and scenario/platform editors operate cohesively.
- [ ] \[OV-SCOPE-01\] Additional theaters remain data-extensible without engine forks.

### OV-SC-N1 — North-Star 5,000+ Entity Interactive FPS and 256x+ Headless AvA Speed (lines 110-112)

Aspirational scale target: realistic 2030-era Baltic scenario with 5,000+ entities at 60+ FPS in Human Mode on recommended hardware and >=256x effective speed in headless Agent-vs-Agent mode.

- [ ] \[OV-SC-N1\] \[Deferred / North-Star\] Headless AvA benchmark achieves >=256x effective simulation speed on an 8 vCPU / 16 GB Linux container.

Aspirational product quality target: agent personality presets are distinguishable in blind After-Action Reviews of AvA batch runs and rated as plausible human command decisions.

Target v1 hardware profiles (Minimum 6-core/16GB/GTX 1660 at 30+ FPS; Recommended 8-core/32GB/RTX 3060 at 60+ FPS with 5,000+ entities; Headless 8 vCPU/16GB Linux container at >=256x floor / 1000x+ target). Scale targets remain north-star/Deferred.

- [ ] \[OV-NFR-04\] \[Deferred / North-Star\] Profiling confirms 30+ FPS on minimum PC spec and 60+ FPS at 5,000+ entities on recommended PC spec.
- [ ] \[OV-NFR-04\] \[Deferred / North-Star\] Linux headless container achieves >=256x effective speed on the reference Baltic scenario.

### OV-SCOPE-02 — Out-of-Scope Later-Release Pillars (Strategic Campaigns, Multiplayer, Tactical Ground) (lines 86-91)

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### DSA-1.1 — Scheduled Daily UTC OSINT Digest Job and Run Summary (lines 33-46)

Run a scheduled daily UTC OSINT digest batch across approved defense/research feeds and persist a structured run summary (sources polled, items found, errors). Headless OsintDigestRunner exists, but scheduled daily UTC execution and run summary persistence remain unproductized.

- [ ] \[DSA-1.1\] Daily digest job completes within configured UTC window and writes a run summary (sources polled, items found, errors).
- [ ] \[DSA-1.1\] Digest job is idempotent and recoverable after partial failure.

### DSA-1.2 — On-Demand MCP OSINT Search Returning Structured Hits (lines 36-47)

Support on-demand targeted OSINT queries via CLI/MCP returning structured discovery records (source URL, snippet, timestamp, relevance score) matching the digest schema. Fixture/RSS CLI and MCP bindings exist, while live external defense/arXiv/patent feed search remains partial.

- [ ] \[DSA-1.2\] On-demand MCP search returns structured hits within the same schema as digest items (source URL, snippet, timestamp, relevance score).

### DSA-1.4 — OSINT Discovery Deduplication Against Staging and Live Catalog IDs (lines 40-49)

Deduplicate each discovered OSINT item against both staging proposals and live database canonical IDs before confidence scoring. Current DedupeDiscoveries only deduplicates within a single digest batch.

- [ ] \[DSA-1.4\] Each discovered item is deduplicated against staging and live DB canonical IDs before scoring.

### DSA-1.5 — Rate-Limit/ToS Compliance and Non-Blocking Source Error Isolation (lines 35-50)

Enforce per-platform rate limits and terms of service across OSINT connectors, logging retrieval failures without blocking subsequent digest runs.

- [ ] \[DSA-1.5\] All retrieval respects platform rate limits and ToS; failures are logged and do not block the next digest.
- [ ] \[DSA-1.5\] Digest and on-demand jobs remain idempotent and recoverable after partial failure.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### DBI-2.1 — Consistent Range and Speed Unit Enum Validation (lines 59-67)

Enforce consistent units and scales across systems (ranges in nm, speeds in knots or Mach) and emit explainable ValidationFinding codes when outside allowed unit enums.

- [ ] \[DBI-2.1\] Validation pipeline flags range/speed unit enums outside allowed sets (nm, knots, Mach) with explainable finding codes.

### DBI-2.2 — Sanity Bounds Enforcement (Max Range > 0, Mach <= 25) (lines 60-68)

Reject or flag commits where max range <= 0 or Mach > 25 per configurable validation defaults. PlatformWorkbook damage/HP bounds exist, while general Mach > 25 and catalog-wide range sanity rules remain incomplete.

- [ ] \[DBI-2.2\] Sanity rules reject or flag commits where max range <= 0 or Mach > 25 (configurable CatalogValidationDefaults).

### DBI-2.4 — Human Approval Gate for >10-Record or Balance-Critical Bulk Commits (lines 63-70)

Require explicit human ApproveBatch confirmation for commits affecting > 10 records or any field tagged balanceCritical to prevent silent bulk normalization.

- [ ] \[DBI-2.4\] P0 commits affecting > 10 records or any balanceCritical field require explicit human ApproveBatch (no silent bulk normalize).

### DBI-3.1 — Referential Integrity Validation for Sensor Bindings (lines 73-84)

Fail/warn validation when sensor bindings reference unknown platformId or sensorId. CatalogRulesValidationAgent and KillChainRules reject unknown platformId on PlatformToSensor edges and missing injected sensors, but lack a sensor master catalog to validate unknown sensorId on CatalogSensorBinding (Run returns Passed=True, Findings=0).

- [ ] \[DBI-3.1\] CatalogRulesValidationAgent fails or warns when sensor bindings reference unknown platformId values (currently covered via KillChainRules KILL_CHAIN_ORPHAN_EDGE).
- [ ] \[DBI-3.1\] CatalogRulesValidationAgent validates sensorId on CatalogSensorBinding against a standalone sensor master catalog/registry and fails or warns on unknown sensorId values.

### DBI-3.4 — Quarantined Binding Isolation Until Explicit Promotion (lines 87-87)

Isolate quarantined bindings (sensor_quarantine) from sim export until promoted. CatalogJsonImporter and SqliteCatalogReader isolate sensor_quarantine from live export, but CatalogQuarantinePromoter.PromoteApproved has 0 production callers in src/unity/CLI and bypasses CatalogWriteGate via raw INSERT OR REPLACE INTO sensor.

- [ ] \[DBI-3.4\] Quarantined bindings (sensor_quarantine table) never appear in live simulation catalog exports until promoted.
- [ ] \[DBI-3.4\] Wire CatalogQuarantinePromoter.PromoteApproved through CatalogWriteGate and MissionEditor.Cli (replacing raw INSERT OR REPLACE INTO sensor SQL) with production callers and CLI tests.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### ARCH-2.2 — Deterministic Runtime TargetRegistry Register/Unregister (lines 102-107)

Support runtime entity registration and unregistration in TargetRegistry without invalidating deterministic tick order. TargetRegistry currently implements RegisterUnit/RegisterGroup with duplicate-key rejection, while runtime Unregister/Remove support is absent from TargetRegistry and DelegationOrchestrator.

- [ ] \[ARCH-2.2\] TargetRegistry exposes runtime Unregister/Remove alongside RegisterUnit/RegisterGroup without invalidating deterministic tick order or corrupting OOB/projection member lists.

### ARCH-2.5 — Managed Entity-Scale Throughput Target (10k-25k @ 1000x+ / 5k @ 60 FPS) (lines 95-110)

Scale managed data-oriented simulation hot paths (SoA, order-stable reductions, optional SIMD) to meet INF-5.1 measurement targets (10,000 v1.0 / 25,000 @ 1000x+ headless / 5,000+ @ 60 FPS interactive presentation).

- [ ] \[ARCH-2.5\] Post-P0: managed entity-scale path meets INF-5.1 measurement bar (ProjectAegis.Sim.Benchmark); map-symbol rendering scale stays in presentation layer.

### ARCH-4.2 — DetectionSubhash Mixing Before Engagement Hash Mix (lines 148-153)

Mix DetectionSubhash via SimTickPipeline.MixDetectionTick before engagement hash update each tick. SimTickPipeline.MixDetectionTick is implemented while BalticReplayHarness/PdDetectionContactSimulator mix externally via DetectionWorldHash.MixTick + SimWorldHash.Combine; MixDetectionTick has 0 callers in src/ and 0 direct tests in SimTickPipelineTests.

- [ ] \[ARCH-4.2\] SimTickPipeline.MixDetectionTick updates DetectionSubhash before engagement hash mix during simulation ticks rather than having 0 production callers.
- [ ] \[ARCH-4.2\] SimTickPipelineTests (and/or session/harness integration tests) directly invoke SimTickPipeline.MixDetectionTick and assert DetectionSubhash updates LastWorldHash prior to engagement hash mixing.

### ARCH-NFR-2 — Analyzer/Gate Ban on [DateTime.Now](<http://DateTime.Now>) and Time.realtimeSinceStartup in Sim (lines 196-196)

Enforce an automated Roslyn analyzer or CI review gate banning [DateTime.Now](<http://DateTime.Now>) and Time.realtimeSinceStartup inside ProjectAegis.Sim. Zero [DateTime.Now](<http://DateTime.Now>) occurrences exist in Sim today, but no automated analyzer/test enforces the ban.

- [ ] \[ARCH-NFR-2\] Ban [DateTime.Now](<http://DateTime.Now>) / Time.realtimeSinceStartup in ProjectAegis.Sim (analyzer or review gate).

### ARCH-AGENTIC-1 — Shared CLI/Optional-MCP Bindings With Zero Shadow Write Paths (lines 200-212)

Expose architecture authoring and batch workflows primarily via ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli with optional Unity-MCP host wrappers sharing the exact same validation and IWriteGate APIs (plus Phase N attribute scaffolding).

- [ ] \[ARCH-AGENTIC-1\] Any MCP host and headless CLI share the same validation and catalog APIs with zero shadow write path.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### ROE-AGENT-01 — Agent policy compliance, Assisted blocked proposals, Swarm Coordinator WRA proposals, and EW Specialist (lines 103-109)

Enforce policy rules on agents (doc 04): block Policy Snapshot violations, prompt Assisted illegal actions with reasons, let Swarm Coordinator propose WRA bumps via PolicyUpdate, and let EwSpecialist prioritize legal jamming/deception. SwarmCoordinator and EwSpecialist presets exist in PersonalityCatalog, while PolicyUpdate proposal loop and EW prioritization remain open.

- [ ] \[ROE-AGENT-01\] Agent controllers never issue orders that violate the active Policy Snapshot, and Assisted mode surfaces blocked agent proposals with abort reasons before confirmation.
- [ ] \[ROE-AGENT-01\] Swarm Coordinator can propose WRA adjustments via PolicyUpdate subject to player or event approval in Assisted+ autonomy.
- [ ] \[ROE-AGENT-01\] Electronic Warfare Specialist prioritizes legal jamming and deception actions strictly within active EMCON and ROE constraints.

### ROE-08 — Editor effective-policy resolution, contradiction validation, and What-If preview (lines 110-126)

Provide Mission Board doctrine/ROE/EMCON editing tabs with inheritance visualization, contradictory-policy validation (e.g., Strike mission with HoldFire), and P1 editor-only What-If rule relaxation preview. Validation tests and DoctrineInheritanceProjection exist, while Mission Board tabs, contradiction checks, and What-If preview remain open.

- [ ] \[ROE-08\] Scenario validation emits deterministic findings for contradictory policies (such as Strike mission paired with HoldFire ROE) alongside DOCTRINE_RESOLVED provenance.
- [ ] \[ROE-08\] Mission Board exposes doctrine/ROE/EMCON inheritance tabs and an editor-test-only What-If preview disabled in ranked play.

### ROE-MCP — Policy MCP and agentic inspection/override tools (lines 149-157)

Expose MCP/CLI verbs policy_get_effective, policy_set_override, policy_explain_fire, and policy_snapshot_list for editor and authorized agent workflows. None of these verbs exist in ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli.

- [ ] \[ROE-MCP\] policy_get_effective, policy_set_override, policy_explain_fire, and policy_snapshot_list are exposed via MissionEditor CLI/MCP with structured JSON output.
- [ ] \[ROE-MCP\] policy_set_override respects policy legality and logs provenance without bypassing PolicySnapshot immutability.

### ROE-NFR — Doctrine/ROE determinism, O(1) evaluation cache, 5k-unit scale, and localization (lines 128-136)

Guarantee deterministic policy evaluation order, O(1) per-mount policy checks with per-tick caching, 5,000+ units with inherited policies without UI stall, and localized string tables for all FireAbortReason descriptions.

- [ ] \[ROE-NFR\] Headless runs with identical PolicySnapshot, world state, and seed produce identical policy denial sequences.
- [ ] \[ROE-NFR\] All FireAbortReason user-facing strings resolve via localization string tables and 5,000+ inherited units render without UI stall.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### LOG-10 — Scenario-level scalar sea-state gate for boat launch and stricter recovery (lines 104-113)

Gate boat launch/recovery using scenario-level Douglas sea-state scalar (0-9) and per-craft maxLaunchSeaState/maxRecoverySeaState. ScenarioSeaState, BoatOpsFsm, BoatOpsStateMap, BoatOpsProjection, and BoatOpsPanelHost exist, but ScenarioMetadataDto and [ProjectAegis.Data/Catalog](<http://ProjectAegis.Data/Catalog>) lack seaState/maxLaunchSeaState/maxRecoverySeaState wiring.

- [ ] \[LOG-10\] Launch is refused with BOAT_NOT_READY:maxLaunchSeaState=<N> when sea state exceeds launch limit.
- [ ] \[LOG-10\] Recovery is refused with BOAT_NOT_READY:maxRecoverySeaState=<N> when sea state exceeds stricter recovery limit, allowing craft launched in rising seas to be blocked from recovery.
- [ ] \[LOG-10\] ScenarioMetadataDto and [ProjectAegis.Data/Catalog](<http://ProjectAegis.Data/Catalog>) (CatalogPlatformEntry/SqliteCatalogReader) deserialize and wire seaStateDouglas, maxLaunchSeaState, and maxRecoverySeaState into SimulationSession.BoatOps.

### LOG-11 — Embarked load capacity, stranded craft persistence, VBSS, and SWARM-13 regen (lines 116-132)

Enforce craft embarked capacity limits, transition abandoned waterborne craft to Stranded with order-log entry, track independent fuel (P2), VBSS boarding (P2), and SWARM-13 host regeneration. Embarked overload refusal and BoatOpsFsm.HostDepartWhileWaterborne->Stranded are shipped, while stranded log rows, craft fuel, VBSS, and SWARM-13 coupling remain open.

- [ ] \[LOG-11\] Overloaded craft refuse launch with EMBARKED_OVERLOAD and waterborne craft whose host departs enter Stranded with a logged order-log row rather than silent destruction.
- [ ] \[LOG-11\] Stranded craft track independent endurance/fuel and support VBSS boarding outcomes and SWARM-13 host-magazine regeneration.

### LOG-MCP — Logistics and magazine MCP tools (lines 207-216)

Expose MCP/CLI verbs logistics_get_readiness, logistics_project_sorties, and magazine_get for inspecting unit readiness breakdowns, sorties-until-bingo projections, and magazine stores/counts. None of these verbs exist in ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli.

- [ ] \[LOG-MCP\] logistics_get_readiness, logistics_project_sorties, and magazine_get are exposed via MissionEditor CLI/MCP with structured JSON output.

### LOG-AGENT-01 — Agent logistics compliance, Swarm Coordinator expendable inventory, LogisticsAbortReason takeoff block, and Cautious boat launch-margin refusal (lines 176-182)

Enforce agent-logistics rules (16:176-182): agents respect bingo/WRA with Cautious early RTB; Swarm Coordinator tracks sub-swarm expendable inventory; P0 blocked takeoff emits LogisticsAbortReason enum; P1 boat launch refuses on sea-state recovery limit (BOAT_NOT_READY), with Cautious refusing at launch margin.

- [ ] \[LOG-AGENT-01\] Agents respect bingo and WRA limits, and Cautious agent personalities return strike assets earlier than Normal/Aggressive under identical fuel/ordnance constraints.
- [ ] \[LOG-AGENT-01\] Swarm Coordinator tracks expendable inventory across sub-swarms deterministically.
- [ ] \[LOG-AGENT-01\] Agent takeoff orders blocked by readiness emit canonical LogisticsAbortReason enum values (P0), and Cautious boat-launch agents refuse at the launch margin with BOAT_NOT_READY rather than waiting for the recovery margin (P1).

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### RPL-06 — Portable replay store bundle and periodic verification checkpoints (lines 88-88)

Persist replay store bundles containing scenario file hash/policy id, catalog version, build id, seed, order log, and periodic verification checkpoints. ReplayCheckpointStore and ReplayCheckpoint are shipped for periodic verification hashes, while portable serialized replay store bundles with build/catalog/scenario metadata remain open.

- [ ] \[RPL-06\] ReplayCheckpointStore records periodic (SimTick, WorldHash, LogFingerprint, LastSequenceId) checkpoints at configurable intervals.
- [ ] \[RPL-06\] Exported replay bundles serialize scenario hash, catalog version, build id, seed, order log, and checkpoints into a self-contained artifact.

### RPL-18 — Running totals for platforms lost, missiles fired, and fuel consumed (lines 112-112)

Compute running totals of platforms lost, missiles fired, and fuel consumed from order-log/logistics records. LossesScoringProjection tallies hostile kills, missiles fired, and denials, while own-side platform losses and fuel-consumed totals remain incomplete.

- [ ] \[RPL-18\] Running totals accurately track friendly/hostile platform losses, missiles fired matching MagazineChange totals, and total fuel consumed matching FuelBurn records.

### RPL-19 — Scenario-metadata scoring model and score-change log events (lines 113-113)

Drive scenario scoring from scenario metadata rules and log event-triggered score changes in the order log. Fixed kill/denial batch scoring exists in LossesScoringProjection, while scenario-configurable scoring rules and logged score-change events remain open.

- [ ] \[RPL-19\] Scenario metadata defines scoring rules and event-triggered score deltas append deterministic score-change entries to the order log.

### RPL-20 — Headless batch CSV export for agent-vs-agent runs (lines 114-114)

Run multi-seed headless batches without UI and export CSV metrics (side, score, losses, sorties, magazine burn rate). BalticBatchRunner and LossesScoringCsvExporter are shipped emitting scenarioId,seed,side,score,kills,missilesFired,denials,fingerprint, while losses, sorties, and magazine burn rate CSV columns remain missing.

- [ ] \[RPL-20\] Headless batch runner executes 100+ runs without UI and exports deterministic CSV metrics per run.
- [ ] \[RPL-20\] LossesScoringCsvExporter includes losses, sorties, and magazine burn rate CSV columns alongside side, score, kills, missilesFired, denials, and fingerprint.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### DOM-06 — Mine domain gate & seeded mine transit hazard (lines 72-84)

Mine domain aspect gate (`MineAspectDomainValidator` / `MINE_ASPECT_BLOCK`) and deterministic seeded mine transit hazard zone (`MineTransitHazardHotTickApplier`). Spine and transit hazard are implemented; mine danger area map presentation and full mine-warfare campaign loop remain open/Phase N.

- [ ] \[DOM-06\] MineAspectDomainValidator blocks out-of-envelope mine domain engagements with MINE_ASPECT_BLOCK when combatDomainsEnabled is true
- [ ] \[DOM-06\] MineTransitHazardHotTickApplier applies deterministic seeded HP damage only when transit coordinates intersect active mine trigger radius
- [ ] \[DOM-06\] Mine danger areas render on C2 map layer (Phase N residual)

### DOM-NFR-01 — Multi-domain determinism, validator skip performance & DB parameter traceability (lines 142-149)

Multi-domain non-functional requirements: seeded sub-RNG per engagement id, zero-cost skip when `combatDomainsEnabled` is false, and catalog source traceability for Phase N fidelity tables.

- [ ] \[DOM-NFR-01\] Domain validators are skipped with zero abort delta when combatDomainsEnabled is false
- [ ] \[DOM-NFR-01\] PK rolls and damage application order remain deterministic across replays from scenario seed
- [ ] \[DOM-NFR-01\] Full fidelity parameters link to catalog source identifiers (Phase N residual)

### DOM-SWARM-01 — Drone swarm integrity-pool damage (`droneCount`) via authorized damage API (lines 188-190)

Drone swarm platforms use integrity-pool damage (`droneCount`) rather than component damage models, routed through the authorized damage API (`ISwarmIntegrityDamageSink`) under air-domain aspect rules (cross-ref SWARM-02/07).

- [ ] \[DOM-SWARM-01\] Engagement hits against swarm targets route integrity reduction through ISwarmIntegrityDamageSink rather than component HP tables
- [ ] \[DOM-SWARM-01\] Air-domain aspect validation applies to swarm engagements without conflating swarms with multi-unit air groups

- [ ] \[COM-DEGRADE-LINK\] DegradeLink degrades the targeted tactical datalink or C2 node for a configured tick duration via deterministic scenario timelines.

- [ ] \[CYB-SWARM-01\] Swarm lost linkState surfaces explicit unknown-with-reason on C2 without inventing zero telemetry
- [ ] \[CYB-SWARM-01\] CEC mesh membership health is modeled independently from tactical datalink and swarm C2 linkState

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### CMD-18 — Domain-appropriate discrete altitude/depth/throttle presets as named commands (lines 91-91)

Altitude/depth and throttle commandable as named doctrinal states per platform domain (e.g., `under_layer`, `creep`, `flank`, `high`) rather than numeric entry alone. `DomainPresetProjection`, `AxisControlPanelHost`, and `AxisControlAndPresetTests` exist on disk; catalog preset backing (doc 06) and end-to-end command dispatch remain open.

- [ ] \[CMD-18\] DomainPresetProjection provides domain-specific named altitude/depth and throttle presets for Air, Surface, and Subsurface units
- [ ] \[CMD-18\] Selecting a named preset dispatches a logged command backed by catalog preset definitions and passes Editor verification

### CMD-19 — Per-axis manual/auto delegation control and mode readout (lines 92-92)

Each commandable axis (altitude/depth, throttle, EMCON, sensors) exposes an independent manual-vs-automatic control and visible mode readout without opening a menu. `AxisControlProjection`, `AxisControlPanelHost`, and `AxisControlAndPresetTests` exist on disk; full ADR-010 sim-to-panel per-axis autonomy state and Editor sign-off remain open.

- [ ] \[CMD-19\] Each commandable axis displays its independent Manual vs Automatic mode directly in the panel without opening a modal/menu
- [ ] \[CMD-19\] Toggling an axis updates per-axis autonomy state via ADR-010 projection/command boundary and reflects Mixed unit status accurately

### CMD-20 — Map distance scale (nm) and camera altitude readout (Phase A baseline) (lines 93-93)

Phase A map baseline displays a nautical-mile distance scale bar and camera altitude readout at every zoom level. `MapScaleProjection`, `MapScaleHudPanelHost`, `CoverageMapScaleEvaluator`, and `MapScaleAndCycleTests` exist on disk; live camera zoom binding and Editor verification remain open.

- [ ] \[CMD-20\] MapScaleProjection computes nautical-mile scale label and camera altitude label deterministically
- [ ] \[CMD-20\] MapScaleHudPanelHost displays updated nm scale bar across zoom changes in Play Mode

### CMD-22 — Top bar scenario date, Zulu time, local time, and remaining duration (lines 95-95)

Top bar renders scenario date, Zulu (`ZULU HH:mm:ss`), local time (`LOCAL HH:mm:ss`), and remaining scenario duration (`REMAIN HH:mm:ss`). `C2TopBarProjection` and `C2TopBarProjectionTests` implement and test these labels headlessly; Unity `C2TopBarPanelHost` binding and Editor verification remain open.

- [ ] \[CMD-22\] C2TopBarProjection formats Zulu, local (with UTC offset), and clamped remaining duration labels from scenario epoch and duration
- [ ] \[CMD-22\] C2TopBarPanelHost displays scenario date, Zulu, local, and remaining duration cleanly in Play Mode

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### PLE-1.2 — Excel enum data-validation dropdowns and \_Meta/PK sheet protection (lines 93-93)

Partial+ (PE-W1 shipped 15 pre-Swarm enum list validations in PlatformWorkbookEnumCatalog + \_Meta/PK sheet locks); Swarms sheet enum/bool columns (DefaultMode, ReviewState, ValueTier, TrlLevel, IsSwarm, RequiresHost, CecCapable) have 0 DV entries and ClosedXmlPlatformWorkbookIo uses XLErrorStyle.Warning.

- [ ] \[PLE-1.2\] Every enum column across all workbook sheets (including Swarms) carries strict Excel data validation restricting input to allowed values.
- [ ] \[PLE-1.2\] ClosedXmlValidationMetadataTests and PlatformWorkbookEnumValidationTests verify enum dropdowns, \_Meta protection, and PK column locks.

### PLE-2.2 — Reject workbook import with unknown or stale SourceSnapshotId (lines 104-104)

Partial+ (PlatformWorkbookImporter rejects unknown \_Meta.SourceSnapshotId where source is null); lacks staleness check rejecting historical snapshots behind the current catalog head.

- [ ] \[PLE-2.2\] PlatformWorkbookImporter rejects workbooks whose \_Meta.SourceSnapshotId is unknown OR stale relative to the current head snapshot with an explainable error.
- [ ] \[PLE-2.2\] PlatformWorkbookImporterTests verify both unknown-snapshot and stale-snapshot rejection.

### PLE-3.3 — Bulk (>10 records) or balanceCritical changes require human ApproveBatch (lines 117-117)

Partial+ (PlatformWorkbookImporter sets informational RequiresHumanApproval for >10-record batches); balanceCritical field detection has 0 hits in src/ (P0 Finding A-02) and CatalogWriteGate.ApproveBatch does not enforce human approval on >10-record or balanceCritical batches.

- [ ] \[PLE-3.3\] Batches touching >10 records or any balanceCritical field return Committed == false and block agent auto-approval in CatalogWriteGate.ApproveBatch until explicit human ApproveBatch is supplied (DBI-2.4).
- [ ] \[PLE-3.3\] Tests verify both >10-record and balanceCritical field human-approval enforcement.

### PLE-4.1 — Unit-enum and physical sanity findings (ValidationFinding) on import (lines 127-127)

Partial+ (PlatformWorkbookValidator flags negative quantities, Emcon.Condition/Posture, and Swarms.DefaultMode); Mach > 25 has 0 hits in [ProjectAegis.Data](<http://ProjectAegis.Data>), checks range < 0 instead of range <= 0, and omits enum checks on MountType, Loadout.Role, Comms.Role, LinkType, ReviewState, ValueTier, and TrlLevel.

- [ ] \[PLE-4.1\] PlatformWorkbookValidator surfaces explainable ValidationFinding codes for range <= 0, Mach > 25, and all unit/provenance enums (MountType, Loadout.Role, Comms.Role, LinkType, ReviewState, ValueTier, TrlLevel).
- [ ] \[PLE-4.1\] PlatformWorkbookValidatorTests cover boundary cases range == 0, Mach > 25, and invalid enum values across all sheets.

Acceptance Criteria:

- [ ] Implement and verify all acceptance criteria for GAP-02, GAP-03, GAP-04, GAP-05 against source spec.

---

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### GAP-02 — missionCode semantic enforcement or explicit non-semantic status (lines 35-41)

Vocabulary-only: ScenarioMissionContactTrigger.MissionCode flows only to MissionTransitionRecord order log with no enum/validation or behavior effect.

- [ ] \[GAP-02\] Either promote missionCode to a validated enum tied to domain/behaviour expectations or explicitly mark/validate it as annotation-only.

### GAP-03 — Weather and sea-state environmental effects on sensors & mobility (lines 46-52)

Absent: no Weather, Precipitation, CloudCover, or Visibility model in src/; envMask is RCS-driven (PhaseBCatalogDetectionModifier). ScenarioSeaState exists only as Douglas 0-9 scalar in BoatOps.

- [ ] \[GAP-03\] Authorable deterministic weather/sea-state model modulating sensor detection (radar/EO/IR), small-craft mobility, and weapon employment without breaking golden hashes unless gated.

### GAP-04 — Terrain, bathymetry, coastline & geometric radar-horizon LOS (lines 53-58)

Partially addressed (LineOfSight.cs / ENV-02 <issue id="c6abedcf-f688-485e-bb59-c648bd12f101" label="DRG-379" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-379/env-02-terrain-and-radar-horizon-line-of-sight" /> landed deterministic authored radar-horizon + terrain profile LOS masking), while full DEM terrain, bathymetry, coastline/land-mask, and submarine depth/bottom constraints remain absent.

- [ ] \[GAP-04\] Full theater bathymetry, coastline/land-mask, and terrain/bottom constraints integrated with detection and movement loops.

### GAP-05 — Acoustic environment (thermocline, CZ, SSP, reverberation) (lines 59-64)

Absent: zero thermocline, convergence zone, sound-speed profile, or acoustic propagation layers; ASW resolves on basic range/Pd.

- [ ] \[GAP-05\] Deterministic acoustic propagation model with layer depth, convergence zones, and depth-dependent detection tested against ASW fixtures.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### KCX-02 — Deterministic Contact Provenance & Source Attribution (lines 65-84)

Project ContactProvenanceState per active contact with Source (ObserverId, TargetId), lifecycle-derived Confidence (High/Medium/Low/Unknown), LastKnown snapshot, QualityState flags, and OutOfCommsUnknown. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[KCX-02\] Fresh contacts publish ObserverId, TargetId, SourceRef, confidence level (Identified->High, Classified/degraded->Medium, Detected->Low), and LastKnown snapshot.
- [ ] \[KCX-02\] A contact whose TargetId is absent from catalog platforms or ORBAT reader sets ContactProvenanceQualityState.CatalogMiss.
- [ ] \[KCX-02\] Denied comms (CommsState.Denied) sets OutOfCommsUnknown=true and ContactProvenanceQualityState.SilentComms.
- [ ] \[KCX-02\] ContactProvenanceFingerprint.Compute produces bit-identical fingerprints across runs for identical inputs.

### KCX-03 — Track Custody, Staleness & Drop Lifecycles (lines 88-100)

Track continuity and custody deterministically via simulation ticks (DefaultStaleThresholdTicks=30, DefaultDropThresholdTicks=120, comms-accelerated staleness), emitting KillChainContactTransition events and TrackCustodyProjection. Draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[KCX-03\] Contact unrefreshed past StaleThresholdTicks (default 30, scaled by comms staleness divisor) transitions to Stale, emitting Degraded transition and breaking Track custody (StaleTrack).
- [ ] \[KCX-03\] Contact unrefreshed past DropThresholdTicks (default 120) transitions to Lost, emitting Lost transition and breaking Sensor link (LostSensor).
- [ ] \[KCX-03\] TrackCustodyProjection records deterministic custody state (Held vs Dropped), drop cause (LostSensor, Stale, CommsDenied, ExplicitDrop, Unknown), and transition ledger.

### KCX-04 — Targetability Composition & Fire-Control Verification (lines 104-117)

Determine contact targetability only when LocationSufficient, TrackContinuous, HasFireControlTrack, and Loss==None all hold, dropping Target phase on BDA degradation while preserving Track custody. Draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[KCX-04\] Identified target with active fire-control assignment publishes Phase=Target and links Targetability in SensorToShooterProjection.
- [ ] \[KCX-04\] Dropping fire-control fails link 3 (Targetability) with BreakCause=NoFireControl while preserving links 1 (Sensor) and 2 (Track).
- [ ] \[KCX-04\] BDA degradation (DegradedL1, DegradedL2) retains TrackContinuous in Phase=Track but drops Phase=Target and breaks Targetability with BreakCause=DegradedTrack.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### KCX-05 — Inspectable Break Causes & Diagnostics Taxonomy (lines 121-139)

Expose standardized SensorToShooterBreakCause codes, user-legible labels, and engagement abort codes (NO_AMMO, DLZ_OUT, ROE_HOLD_FIRE) consumed read-only by UI per ADR-010. Draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[KCX-05\] Every failed 4-link chain reports a canonical SensorToShooterBreakCause enum value and standard display label (lost sensor, stale track, no FC, no eligible shooter, degraded track).
- [ ] \[KCX-05\] Eligible shooter evaluation exposes underlying abort codes (NO_AMMO, DLZ_OUT, ROE_HOLD_FIRE) and falls back across candidate shooters before breaking the link.
- [ ] \[KCX-05\] UI components consume these labels read-only per ADR-010 without re-deriving break causes.

### KCX-06 — Identity & Standard Classification Ledger (lines 143-154)

Maintain deterministic contact identity across kill-chain phases (None->Find->Fix->Track->Target), immutable transitions, MIL-STD-2525/APP-6 standard identity (App6Sidc), and IdentityClassProjection reason codes. Draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[KCX-06\] Phase changes emit immutable KillChainContactTransition events with PreviousPhase, NewPhase, SimTick, SimTime, and sequence ID.
- [ ] \[KCX-06\] App6Sidc deterministically resolves standard identity (F, N, H, S, P, U) from contact classification without leaking hidden identity.
- [ ] \[KCX-06\] IdentityClassProjection projects IdentityClassification (Unknown, Tentative, Classified, Identified) with explicit IdentityClassReasonCodes.

### KCX-07 — Threat Assessment & Next-Action Diagnostics (lines 158-172)

Project strictly advisory WeaponRecommendation outcomes (Feasible, WithheldByPolicy, WithheldByEngage) via ThreatAssessmentProjection and ReloadRearm/Approval guidance via EngageNextActionProjection. Draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[KCX-07\] Threat evaluation under RoeLevel.WeaponsTight outputs Outcome=WithheldByPolicy, WithheldReasonCode=ROE_WEAPONS_TIGHT, and non-null StatusLine.
- [ ] \[KCX-07\] Out-of-DLZ or zero-ammo engagements output Outcome=WithheldByEngage with explicit reason code even under WeaponsFree.
- [ ] \[KCX-07\] WeaponRecommendation enforces IsWeaponsReleaseAuthorization=false, IsFireOrder=false, IsAutomaticEngagement=false.
- [ ] \[KCX-07\] EngageNextActionProjection emits deterministic ReloadRearm or Approval guidance with IsFireOrder=false.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### KCX-05 — Inspectable Break Causes & Diagnostics Taxonomy (lines 121-139)

Expose standardized SensorToShooterBreakCause codes, user-legible labels, and engagement abort codes (NO_AMMO, DLZ_OUT, ROE_HOLD_FIRE) consumed read-only by UI per ADR-010. Draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[KCX-05\] Every failed 4-link chain reports a canonical SensorToShooterBreakCause enum value and standard display label (lost sensor, stale track, no FC, no eligible shooter, degraded track).
- [ ] \[KCX-05\] Eligible shooter evaluation exposes underlying abort codes (NO_AMMO, DLZ_OUT, ROE_HOLD_FIRE) and falls back across candidate shooters before breaking the link.
- [ ] \[KCX-05\] UI components consume these labels read-only per ADR-010 without re-deriving break causes.

### KCX-06 — Identity & Standard Classification Ledger (lines 143-154)

Maintain deterministic contact identity across kill-chain phases (None->Find->Fix->Track->Target), immutable transitions, MIL-STD-2525/APP-6 standard identity (App6Sidc), and IdentityClassProjection reason codes. Draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[KCX-06\] Phase changes emit immutable KillChainContactTransition events with PreviousPhase, NewPhase, SimTick, SimTime, and sequence ID.
- [ ] \[KCX-06\] App6Sidc deterministically resolves standard identity (F, N, H, S, P, U) from contact classification without leaking hidden identity.
- [ ] \[KCX-06\] IdentityClassProjection projects IdentityClassification (Unknown, Tentative, Classified, Identified) with explicit IdentityClassReasonCodes.

### KCX-07 — Threat Assessment & Next-Action Diagnostics (lines 158-172)

Project strictly advisory WeaponRecommendation outcomes (Feasible, WithheldByPolicy, WithheldByEngage) via ThreatAssessmentProjection and ReloadRearm/Approval guidance via EngageNextActionProjection. Draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[KCX-07\] Threat evaluation under RoeLevel.WeaponsTight outputs Outcome=WithheldByPolicy, WithheldReasonCode=ROE_WEAPONS_TIGHT, and non-null StatusLine.
- [ ] \[KCX-07\] Out-of-DLZ or zero-ammo engagements output Outcome=WithheldByEngage with explicit reason code even under WeaponsFree.
- [ ] \[KCX-07\] WeaponRecommendation enforces IsWeaponsReleaseAuthorization=false, IsFireOrder=false, IsAutomaticEngagement=false.
- [ ] \[KCX-07\] EngageNextActionProjection emits deterministic ReloadRearm or Approval guidance with IsFireOrder=false.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### HOL-02 — Pending Approval Queue & Execution Gate (lines 92-97)

Maintain session-local PendingApprovalQueue for orders flagged GateResult.QueueForApproval (plus EscalationGateProjection), enforcing explicit human approval before execution. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[HOL-02\] Orders enqueued to PendingApprovalQueue MUST NOT execute until explicitly approved via TryApprove(orderId).
- [ ] \[HOL-02\] Rejection via TryReject(orderId) MUST remove the entry without execution.
- [ ] \[HOL-02\] Approved orders drain via DrainApproved() and promote to ExecutedOrders on the subsequent simulation tick.
- [ ] \[HOL-02\] Queue operations MUST be idempotent; duplicate OrderId submissions MUST be ignored.

### HOL-03 — C2 Authority & Targeting Disposition Projection (lines 99-104)

Project ROE, track source, fire-control status, and required approval into explicit dispositions (Permitted, Withheld, ApprovalRequired) across the six core action verbs via C2AuthorityProjector. Draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[HOL-03\] When RoeLevel is HoldFire or WeaponsTight, targeting disposition MUST be Withheld (RoeHoldFire or WeaponsTight).
- [ ] \[HOL-03\] When track source is DatalinkShared or FusedWithoutOrganicFc, targeting disposition MUST be Withheld (SHARED_TRACK_NO_RELEASE, ADR-018).
- [ ] \[HOL-03\] When RequiredApproval is Operator or WeaponsRelease, disposition MUST be ApprovalRequired with corresponding reason codes.
- [ ] \[HOL-03\] All six core verbs (Observe, Recommend, Approve, Engage, Abort, Retask) MUST receive an explicit C2AuthorityActionState.

### HOL-05 — Agent C2 Skill Contract & Envelopes (lines 112-116)

Enforce structured skill envelope validation (SkillEnvelopeValidator, SkillCatalog, SkillIds) across segregated Read, Propose, and Submit lanes against known C2CommandIssuance verbs. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[HOL-05\] Every envelope MUST declare lane (Read, Propose, or Submit), skillId, invocationId, and time credentials (simTick, simTime).
- [ ] \[HOL-05\] Propose and submit envelopes MUST include authorityBasis, requiredApproval, playerOverride, and evidence pointers.
- [ ] \[HOL-05\] SkillEnvelopeValidator MUST validate command IDs against known C2CommandIssuance verbs and reject malformed envelopes.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### HOL-02 — Pending Approval Queue & Execution Gate (lines 92-97)

Maintain session-local PendingApprovalQueue for orders flagged GateResult.QueueForApproval (plus EscalationGateProjection), enforcing explicit human approval before execution. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[HOL-02\] Orders enqueued to PendingApprovalQueue MUST NOT execute until explicitly approved via TryApprove(orderId).
- [ ] \[HOL-02\] Rejection via TryReject(orderId) MUST remove the entry without execution.
- [ ] \[HOL-02\] Approved orders drain via DrainApproved() and promote to ExecutedOrders on the subsequent simulation tick.
- [ ] \[HOL-02\] Queue operations MUST be idempotent; duplicate OrderId submissions MUST be ignored.

### HOL-03 — C2 Authority & Targeting Disposition Projection (lines 99-104)

Project ROE, track source, fire-control status, and required approval into explicit dispositions (Permitted, Withheld, ApprovalRequired) across the six core action verbs via C2AuthorityProjector. Draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[HOL-03\] When RoeLevel is HoldFire or WeaponsTight, targeting disposition MUST be Withheld (RoeHoldFire or WeaponsTight).
- [ ] \[HOL-03\] When track source is DatalinkShared or FusedWithoutOrganicFc, targeting disposition MUST be Withheld (SHARED_TRACK_NO_RELEASE, ADR-018).
- [ ] \[HOL-03\] When RequiredApproval is Operator or WeaponsRelease, disposition MUST be ApprovalRequired with corresponding reason codes.
- [ ] \[HOL-03\] All six core verbs (Observe, Recommend, Approve, Engage, Abort, Retask) MUST receive an explicit C2AuthorityActionState.

### HOL-05 — Agent C2 Skill Contract & Envelopes (lines 112-116)

Enforce structured skill envelope validation (SkillEnvelopeValidator, SkillCatalog, SkillIds) across segregated Read, Propose, and Submit lanes against known C2CommandIssuance verbs. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[HOL-05\] Every envelope MUST declare lane (Read, Propose, or Submit), skillId, invocationId, and time credentials (simTick, simTime).
- [ ] \[HOL-05\] Propose and submit envelopes MUST include authorityBasis, requiredApproval, playerOverride, and evidence pointers.
- [ ] \[HOL-05\] SkillEnvelopeValidator MUST validate command IDs against known C2CommandIssuance verbs and reject malformed envelopes.

### HOL-06 — Advisory Threat Assessment & Weapon Recommendation (HOL Boundary) (lines 118-123)

Ensure headless ThreatAssessmentProjection evaluates DLZ range, magazine state, mount status, and doctrine purely as an advisory recommendation without issuing fire orders. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[HOL-06\] WeaponRecommendation MUST explicitly assert IsWeaponsReleaseAuthorization=false, IsFireOrder=false, and IsAutomaticEngagement=false.
- [ ] \[HOL-06\] Outcomes MUST classify into Feasible, WithheldByPolicy, or WithheldByEngage.
- [ ] \[HOL-06\] Recommendations MUST include human-readable assumptions, DLZ range assessment, policy constraints, confidence score, and status line.
- [ ] \[HOL-06\] ComputeFingerprint MUST produce deterministic, replay-stable fingerprints across runs given identical inputs.

### HOL-07 — Resource Scarcity Ranking & Weapon Pairing (lines 125-130)

Evaluate and rank candidate shooter/weapon pairings under scarcity constraints via ResourceRankProjection using five deterministic weights without authorizing weapons release. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[HOL-07\] ResourceRankSnapshot MUST assert IsWeaponsReleaseAuthorization=false, IsFireOrder=false, and IsAutomaticEngagement=false.
- [ ] \[HOL-07\] Candidates MUST be scored using weights: Expected Effect (0.35), Time-to-Effect (0.20), Round Availability (0.20), Commitment (0.15), Magazine Conservation (0.10).
- [ ] \[HOL-07\] Candidates MUST categorize into Preferred (rank 1), Alternative (rank 2+), or Excluded with explicit reason codes.
- [ ] \[HOL-07\] ComputeFingerprint MUST produce a deterministic fingerprint string.

### HOL-08 — Collateral Damage Estimation (CDE) & Advisory Withhold (lines 132-136)

Project advisory collateral risk levels (Low, Elevated, Withheld), range classes, and policy denials via CdeAssessProjection without issuing fire authorizations. Headless subset exists; draft pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[HOL-08\] CdeAssessSnapshot MUST be strictly advisory and MUST NOT emit weapons release or fire authorizations.
- [ ] \[HOL-08\] Risk MUST categorize as Low, Elevated, or Withheld (explicit collateral withhold or shooter-scoped policy denials).
- [ ] \[HOL-08\] Projections MUST record explicit assumptions regarding engage preview, policy denial records, and CDE withhold status.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### C2N-01 — C2 Nodes & Mission Package Composition (lines 42-75)

Support authored multi-platform PackageDefinition mission packages with C2NodeRole, C2NodeMembershipKind, and C2NodeAvailability projected via MissionPackageProjection. Headless subset (<issue id="b559089d-eae1-42ef-afba-73b3549323af" label="DRG-213" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-213/slice-a-headless-c2-nodes-and-mission-packages" />) landed; draft maturity retained pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[C2N-01\] Pure projection outside tick hotpath folds platform alive state, damage records, detach/rejoin status, and comms state without dropping dead platforms from membership.
- [ ] \[C2N-01\] Denied comms marks Relay/C2 package elements Unavailable and degraded comms marks them LastKnown, while Organic capabilities remain Available.
- [ ] \[C2N-01\] MissionPackageProjection.ComputeFingerprint yields identical SHA-256 digests regardless of definition ordering.

### C2N-02 — C2 Network Health & Mesh Partition Assessment (lines 79-103)

Project real-time friendly C2 network health (Healthy, Degraded, Partitioned), link rows, PartitionedUnits, LastKnownContributors, and LostPaths via C2NetworkHealthProjector. Headless subset (<issue id="c0e5d43d-beb2-4e0d-808e-5249d6bf7744" label="DRG-214" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-214/slice-a-headless-c2-network-health-projection" />) landed; draft maturity retained pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[C2N-02\] Fully connected meshes project Healthy; single link failures identify PartitionedUnits; degraded/denied comms yield Degraded/Partitioned; LinkStatusOverride forces partition or recovery.
- [ ] \[C2N-02\] C2NetworkHealthFingerprint.Compute produces identical strings for equivalent snapshots and diverges when the mesh partitions.

### C2N-04 — Mission Command Intent & Degraded Operations (lines 132-159)

Project commander guidance (Hold, Attack, Withdraw), active constraints, and advisory retask advice via MissionIntentProjection (<issue id="b842288e-371c-469b-b81e-2e3e0f33b53d" label="DRG-229" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-229/slice-c-headless-mission-command-intent-and-constraint-dto" />) without emitting orders. Headless subset landed; draft maturity retained pending owner acceptance.

- [ ] \[C2N-04\] MissionIntentProjection.Project produces read-only AdvisoryIntent snapshots with IsOrder=false, IsWeaponsReleaseAuthorization=false, IsFireOrder=false, IsAutomaticEngagement=false.
- [ ] \[C2N-04\] Constrained intents accurately reflect active constraints and advisory retask recommendations without generating direct execution orders.
- [ ] \[C2N-04\] MissionIntentProjection.ComputeFingerprint produces stable deterministic fingerprints.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### AGD-04 — Four Autonomy Levels with ROE/Policy Gate and Lethal Opt-In (lines 32-39)

Implement four autonomy levels (Manual, Assisted, SemiAutonomous, FullAutonomous) integrated with ROE/policy evaluation (AutonomyGate + RoePolicyAdapter), requiring explicit player opt-in per mission phase for full-autonomous lethal engagement.

- [ ] \[AGD-04\] AutonomyLevel defines Manual, Assisted, SemiAutonomous, and FullAutonomous tiers gated by AutonomyGate and IRoeFilter.
- [ ] \[AGD-04\] Full autonomous lethal engagement enforces explicit player opt-in per mission phase (aligned with PendingApprovalQueue / HOL).

### AGD-07 — Realistic Variability via Deterministic Trait-Weighted Softmax DecisionPipeline (lines 60-63)

Exhibit human-like decision variability (mistakes, hesitation, personality styles). DecisionPipeline softmax (Decisiveness), SeededRng, SlowerReactions (ReactionDelay\*5), and NarrowedFocus (Take(2)) are shipped, while ErrorRate, Aggression, and RiskTolerance candidate scoring remain unwired across DecisionPipeline and IPolicy implementations.

- [ ] \[AGD-07\] DecisionPipeline selects among candidate actions deterministically using SeededRng given identical seed, traits, candidates, and attention state.
- [ ] \[AGD-07\] ErrorRate (occasional mistakes), Aggression, and RiskTolerance drive candidate scoring and personality-specific decision styles in IPolicy/DecisionPipeline rather than remaining unwired.

### AGD-09 — Agent Delegation Responsiveness, Logging, and ROE Compliance NFRs (lines 69-75)

Ensure delegation remains responsive at thousands of entities without performance degradation, logs 100% of agent decisions for replay, and strictly respects ROE and player-defined constraints.

- [ ] \[AGD-09\] All agent intents pass through AutonomyGate and IRoeFilter before execution.
- [ ] \[AGD-09\] Delegation tick overhead remains bounded as entity count scales.

### AGD-11 — Agent Attention and Bandwidth Model with Graceful Degradation (lines 136-144)

Enforce per-agent attention budget (default 20, personality-modulated) scaling load by contacts/engagements/groups and degrading overloaded decisions. AttentionCalculator, SlowerReactions, and NarrowedFocus + IsOverloaded temperature scaling are shipped, while SimplerDecisions (>1.5x budget) is UI-only and overload integration tests are missing.

- [ ] \[AGD-11\] AttentionCalculator computes load from contacts, engagements, and group members against personality-modulated budget (default 20), with SlowerReactions and NarrowedFocus active.
- [ ] \[AGD-11\] SimplerDecisions drives simpler decision behavior in AgentController/DecisionPipeline (beyond UI projection) and overload degradation is covered by integration tests beyond AttentionCalculator.Evaluate.

### AGD-14 — Delegation Comms Degradation and Attention Coupling (lines 106-106)

Integrate CommsTimelineSimulator order delays and stale/datalink flags into agent observations and reduce effective attention budget under degraded comms (Phase 2), with EW Specialist preset balancing comms/EMCON tradeoffs.

- [ ] \[AGD-14\] Agents observe stale/datalink status flags from comms timelines without breaking determinism.
- [ ] \[AGD-14\] Degraded comms modulates effective attention budget per doc 19 integration.

## Requirement Breakdown & Detailed Acceptance Criteria

### AGD-04 — Four Autonomy Levels with ROE/Policy Gate and Lethal Opt-In (lines 32-39)

Implement four autonomy levels (Manual, Assisted, SemiAutonomous, FullAutonomous) integrated with ROE/policy evaluation (AutonomyGate + RoePolicyAdapter), requiring explicit player opt-in per mission phase for full-autonomous lethal engagement.

- [ ] \[AGD-04\] AutonomyLevel defines Manual, Assisted, SemiAutonomous, and FullAutonomous tiers gated by AutonomyGate and IRoeFilter.
- [ ] \[AGD-04\] Full autonomous lethal engagement enforces explicit player opt-in per mission phase (aligned with PendingApprovalQueue / HOL).

### AGD-07 — Realistic Variability via Deterministic Trait-Weighted Softmax DecisionPipeline (lines 60-63)

Exhibit human-like decision variability (mistakes, hesitation, personality styles). DecisionPipeline softmax (Decisiveness), SeededRng, SlowerReactions (ReactionDelay\*5), and NarrowedFocus (Take(2)) are shipped, while ErrorRate, Aggression, and RiskTolerance candidate scoring remain unwired across DecisionPipeline and IPolicy implementations.

- [ ] \[AGD-07\] DecisionPipeline selects among candidate actions deterministically using SeededRng given identical seed, traits, candidates, and attention state.
- [ ] \[AGD-07\] ErrorRate (occasional mistakes), Aggression, and RiskTolerance drive candidate scoring and personality-specific decision styles in IPolicy/DecisionPipeline rather than remaining unwired.

### AGD-09 — Agent Delegation Responsiveness, Logging, and ROE Compliance NFRs (lines 69-75)

Ensure delegation remains responsive at thousands of entities without performance degradation, logs 100% of agent decisions for replay, and strictly respects ROE and player-defined constraints.

- [ ] \[AGD-09\] All agent intents pass through AutonomyGate and IRoeFilter before execution.
- [ ] \[AGD-09\] Delegation tick overhead remains bounded as entity count scales.

### AGD-11 — Agent Attention and Bandwidth Model with Graceful Degradation (lines 136-144)

Enforce per-agent attention budget (default 20, personality-modulated) scaling load by contacts/engagements/groups and degrading overloaded decisions. AttentionCalculator, SlowerReactions, and NarrowedFocus + IsOverloaded temperature scaling are shipped, while SimplerDecisions (>1.5x budget) is UI-only and overload integration tests are missing.

- [ ] \[AGD-11\] AttentionCalculator computes load from contacts, engagements, and group members against personality-modulated budget (default 20), with SlowerReactions and NarrowedFocus active.
- [ ] \[AGD-11\] SimplerDecisions drives simpler decision behavior in AgentController/DecisionPipeline (beyond UI projection) and overload degradation is covered by integration tests beyond AttentionCalculator.Evaluate.

### AGD-14 — Delegation Comms Degradation and Attention Coupling (lines 106-106)

Integrate CommsTimelineSimulator order delays and stale/datalink flags into agent observations and reduce effective attention budget under degraded comms (Phase 2), with EW Specialist preset balancing comms/EMCON tradeoffs.

- [ ] \[AGD-14\] Agents observe stale/datalink status flags from comms timelines without breaking determinism.
- [ ] \[AGD-14\] Degraded comms modulates effective attention budget per doc 19 integration.
